title: Conditions for Booking a Companion Trip — Crestline Companion Certificates and Passes
content:
A companion trip on Crestline Companion Certificates and Passes is booked only when every condition below holds. Each condition is read from the system records of the certificate or pass being used and of the holder's Summit membership linked to it, not from the customer's account of them.

## A. Status of the certificate or pass

A companion trip can be booked only while the certificate or pass is active. A product that is issued, used, expired or revoked takes no booking.

## B. The book-by date

A companion trip can be booked only on or before the book-by date shown on the certificate or pass. The book-by date is inclusive and counted in calendar days in US Central time; when the product requires travel to be completed by the book-by date, every companion flight must also depart on or before it.

- The clock is the booking day, as a calendar day in US Central time, compared with the book-by date shown on that certificate or pass.
- The comparison is not later than: a booking on the book-by date itself is on time.
- There is no grace period: 0 calendar days are allowed after the book-by date.

| Hypothetical booking day (US Central) against a book-by date of 31 October | Can the trip be booked? |
|---|---|
| 30 October | yes |
| 31 October, at any hour of that calendar day | yes (the date is inclusive) |
| 1 November | no |

## C. The holder's Summit membership

A companion trip is booked only when the holder's Summit membership is not closed: its status on record must be enrolled, active or dormant.

## D. Travelers, fares and routing

- The holder must travel as primary passenger where the product requires it, and the companion must be on the same reservation and flights where the product requires it.
- Both are ticketed in one of the product's eligible fare brands in the same cabin, never on partner flights, and the holder never on an award ticket.
- The itinerary must be within the product's route scope, where domestic and short-haul adds short-haul international itineraries and travel to or from Hawaii counts as domestic only when the product makes Hawaii eligible.
- No companion flight may depart inside the product's blackout periods, no direction may have more than the product's most segments per direction, and the trip must be booked at least the product's advance-booking minimum in calendar days before its first departure.

## E. Designated companion on a pass

A pass must have a designated companion name before any booking where the product requires designation, and only that person may travel as its companion.

## F. Monthly limit

The trips booked for one travel month may not exceed the product's monthly trip limit. The count is taken over the calendar month of the travel date of the trip being booked: every companion booking on the same certificate or pass whose travel date falls in that month, less those later reinstated.

**Hypothetical example.** A pass with a monthly limit of 2 already carries three bookings with travel dates in May, one of which was later reinstated. The count for May is 2, so a further trip travelling in May cannot be booked; a trip travelling in June can.
